- When sentiment turns negative in the recent history, reduce forecasted price momentum and avoid over-optimistic spikes.  
- If model forecast shows a sharp upward spike followed by a steep decline in true outcome, cap future forecasts at the recent 5-day moving average to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative signals (e.g., -1.00 for 3+ consecutive days), apply a downward bias of 1–2% to the forecast mean.  
- When true outcome consistently underperforms model forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), adjust for mean reversion by applying a 1–3% downward correction to the next 5-day forecast.  
- If model forecast is significantly higher than recent 10-day average (e.g., >15% above), reduce forecast by 5–10% to account for overconfidence bias.  
- For forecasts with high volatility in sentiment (e.g., alternating +1/-1), apply a smoothing filter to dampen extreme swings in the 30-day forecast.
